newsitem.title: UK: British security sources deny Sinn Fein chief held.
newsitem.headline: British security sources deny Sinn Fein chief held.

text.p: British security sources on Thursday denied that Gerry Adams, president of the Irish Republican Army's Sinn Fein political wing, had been arrested.
Sinn Fein said earlier that Adams and party colleague Gerry Kelly had been detained by the army near Belfast.
Northern Ireland police declined to comment on the case, saying: "It's not our policy to discuss security matters."
But security sources said Adams and Kelly had not been detained or arrested.
"They were never arrested and are not currently detained," a security source said.
Sinn Fein said the pair were held by British troops near Banbridge in Northern Ireland's County Down, south of Belfast.
The party said Adams and Kelly were held and "generally harassed" by British army soldiers.
Sinn Fein said the two men were on their way back to Belfast from a party meeting.
